data.long_meaning: From Sanskrit 'mitra' meaning friend, ally, or supporter. In Hindu mythology, Mitra is a deity associated with friendship, oaths, and contracts. The name Mit carries the meaning “Friend” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Mit usually hope their child will grow to embody friend and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Mit stems from its connection to the Hindu deity, Mitra, who symbolizes the profound bond between individuals. Through this, the name Mit carries a spiritual reminder of the importance of nurturing relationships and keeping promises.

historical_references.context: Mitra and Varuna were two ancient gods worshipped in the Rigveda. They were believed to be friends and upholders of truth, justice, and order. The Mitra-Varuna friendship pact was a ritual agreement sworn by two parties to establish a bond of friendship, trust, and mutual cooperation. It is mentioned in several hymns and invocations in the Rigveda.

historical_references.context: Mitrasa Devanayaka was a ruler of the Satavahana Dynasty, which ruled large parts of ancient India from the 3rd century BCE to the 3rd century CE. He is mentioned in the inscription found at the site of the temple of Amaravati, Andhra Pradesh, India. The inscription dates back to circa 150-200 CE and commemorates Mitrasa's donation to the temple.
